title: The Well-Tempered Clavier, Book 2, Fugue 11 in F major

character.text: Light gigue-type partimento fugue, without learned devices

sections.label: Episode 1
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject. Alto: free counterpoint. Bass: a figure from the subject. Returns in Episode 2 (bars 25–51).

sections.label: Episode 2
sections.summary: Reworks Episode 1 (bars 18–20) in part, with alto and bass exchanged, the lines moved by different intervals (invertible counterpoint at the twelfth). Soprano: a figure from the subject (6 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence rising by a third every two bars. Alto: a figure from the subject (5 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times), in a sequence rising by a third every two bars. Bass: a figure from the subject (7 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times), in a sequence rising by a third every two bars.

sections.label: Episode 3
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: free counterpoint, in a sequence falling by a fifth every bar.

sections.label: Episode 4
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject (3 times) and the opening of the subject, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Alto: a figure from the subject (2 times) and a figure from the subject, inverted, in a sequence falling by a step every bar. Bass: a figure from the subject (3 times) and the opening of the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every bar.

sections.label: Subject in F major, rhythm varied (Bass)
Episode 5
sections.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted. Bass: a figure from the subject, inverted (2 times) and a figure from the subject, in a sequence rising by a step every bar.

spans.label: Codetta
spans.summary: Soprano: a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times) and a figure from the subject. Alto: a figure from the subject, inverted (3 times) and a figure from the subject.
